To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the antimicrobial agent fusidic is a potent inhibitor of organic anion transporting peptide 1B1 and organic anion transporting protein 1B3, which may potentiate the myopathic effects of statin drugs.
FA, a bacteriostatic antibiotic, inhibits human OATP-mediated hepatic clearance of statins and may potentiate statin-induced myopathy.
fusidic acid is a weak inhibitor of CYP450 3A4 and a potent inhibitor of OATP-mediated statin uptake.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of FA as an inhibitor of human OATPs, which may contribute to the increased risk of statin-induced myopathy when coadministered with FA.
the identification of a potential mechanism for the development of statin-induced myopathy in patients treated with FA.
the inhibition of OATPs by the antibacterial agent FA and the potential for adverse drug–drug interactions with statins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inhibition of human hepatic transporters, particularly OATP1Bs, by FA is the most probable cause of the observed clinical myopathy.
coadministration of FA and statins should be avoided because of potential adverse effects on musculoskeletal toxicity, and FA should be considered a new substrate of OATP transporters.
the potent inhibitory effects of the antimicrobial agent FA on the hepatic uptake transporters OATP1A4, OATP1a4, OAT1b2, and OATP2B1 may be a contributing factor to statin-induced myopathy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fusidic acid is a weak CYP3A inhibitor and a potent OATP inhibitor and could potentially increase statin exposure and potentiate statin-related myopathy.
FA inhibits CYP3A, OATP1, and MDR1, and these effects could contribute to the myopathy observed in patients taking statins and FA.
FA is a weak reversible inhibitor and a potent time-dependent inhibitor of CYP 3A4.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FA is a potent inhibitor of the hepatic uptake transporter OATP1b1 and OAT1b3, which are responsible to uptake of statins.
FA is a potent inhibitor of OATP-mediated hepatic uptake of rosuvastatin.
coadministration of statins with FA may potentiate the development of statin-induced myopathy.
